claim: A Type I genitive determiner marks the whole containing NP as definite.
evidence_summary: An indefinite possessor can introduce a new dog. A listener can also accommodate a salient dog relative to that possessor.
finding: Test whole-NP uniqueness and quantification against competing accounts. The article on the possessor is insufficient evidence.
inference: Does marking the possessor’s relation determine the definiteness of the whole possessive?

evidence.source: Elizabeth Coppock & David Beaver (2015). Definiteness and determinacy. Linguistics and Philosophy 38(5), 377–435.
evidence.passage: §4, p. 357. A Type I genitive determiner marks the whole containing NP as definite.
evidence.example: The authors distinguish properties that are easily conflated in claims about what a definite form contributes.
evidence.establishes: A theoretical comparison. Testing the whole possessive still requires opposing predictions in the same context.
evidence.locator: The distinction between definiteness and determinacy.

evidence.source: Peter Willemse (2007). Indefinite possessive NPs and the distinction between determining and nondetermining genitives in English. English Language & Linguistics 11(3), 537–568.

evidence.example: The study distinguishes uses within possessive expressions that can look alike in isolation.
evidence.establishes: Motivates controlling which possessive construction is at issue before inferring whole-NP definiteness.
evidence.locator: Analysis of determining and nondetermining genitives.
